question: What is the main goal of a descriptive research design?

options.A: To prove a direct cause-and-effect relationship between two treatments
options.B: To accurately describe a situation or population without changing variables
options.C: To test a new medical drug against a standard placebo
options.D: To manipulate patient routines and measure the physical outcome

explanation: Think of descriptive research like taking a clear photograph: you are just capturing things exactly as they are in real life without meddling or changing anything. Great job! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why must a nurse researcher use a descriptive design before starting an experimental trial?

options.A: Because descriptive data helps establish basic baseline knowledge about a problem
options.B: Because ethical boards legally forbid any nursing experiments without surveys
options.C: Because descriptive designs are the only way to get funding from hospitals
options.D: Because experiments always fail if they do not include a questionnaire

explanation: You cannot fix a problem if you don't first understand it! Descriptive work gives us that essential starting picture before we try out new treatments. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which feature is always true about a descriptive research study?

options.A: The researcher does not manipulate any variables
options.B: The study must take place inside a sterile laboratory
options.C: Only one person is observed at a time

explanation: In descriptive studies, researchers take a hands-off approach. They observe and record without altering or tampering with anything. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h2)

question: What role do descriptive studies play in nursing science?

options.A: They supply baseline facts that point toward areas needing clinical investigation
options.B: They replace clinical trials by proving which drugs cure diseases
options.C: They force patients to alter their daily health habits for better outcomes
options.D: They eliminate all errors found in previous medical journals

explanation: Descriptive studies act like our radar—they highlight where health issues lie, guiding nurses on what needs closer study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h2)

question: What is the main characteristic of a cross-sectional descriptive study?

options.A: The researcher changes the patient's diet plan
options.B: Data is collected at one specific point in time
options.C: Only one patient is ever studied at a time
options.D: Participants are followed continuously for many years

explanation: Think of a cross-sectional study as a quick snapshot—it gathers information from a group at one single moment, with no long-term follow-up. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h3)

question: A nursing team wants to track how post-surgery mobility changes in elderly patients over the course of one year. Which design fits best?
explanation: When you want to watch patients grow, heal, or change over a long period (like a year), a longitudinal study is your go-to choice! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which tool is most frequently used to gather opinions from large groups in descriptive research?
explanation: When you need to hear from many people quickly, questionnaires and surveys are the easiest and most practical tools to use. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h4)

question: A nurse researcher wants to study patient hygiene habits in a ward without changing their routine. What is the most suitable data collection approach?
explanation: To see how people naturally behave without them putting on an act, direct observation in their real environment works best. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h4)

question: What must be obtained before starting data collection with human participants in a study?

options.C: A patent for a new drug

explanation: Patient safety and rights always come first. Ethical approval ensures your study is safe and respects human dignity. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why is proper sampling important when conducting a descriptive survey in a hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that every single patient in the country will be cured
options.B: It removes the need to analyze numerical data at the end
options.C: It stops patients from answering survey questions incorrectly
options.D: It ensures the selected group accurately reflects the entire patient population

explanation: Good sampling means the few people you study are a true mini-version of the whole group, making your findings reliable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which of the following is an example of a descriptive statistic?

options.B: The exact biological cause of a virus mutation
options.C: A proven cure rate for a genetic disorder
options.D: Percentage of patients with high blood pressure

explanation: Numbers like percentages, averages, and counts are classic descriptive statistics that simply summarize what is happening in the data. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is a common error when interpreting results from a descriptive study?

options.A: Using percentages to explain how many participants answered a survey
options.B: Concluding that one variable caused another simply because they occurred together
options.C: Creating a bar chart to display age groups in the sample
options.D: Comparing current findings with past published nursing literature

explanation: Just because two things happen at the same time doesn't mean one caused the other! Descriptive studies show connections, not direct causes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of descriptive research designs?

options.B: They cannot use questionnaires or interviews
options.C: They are too expensive for ordinary nursing students

explanation: Because descriptive studies don't involve testing or experiments, they can only tell you what is happening, not why it is strictly causing something else. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of descriptive research?

options.A: Generating useful baseline data for future studies
options.B: Providing a clear picture of health habits in a community
options.C: Proving definitively which nursing intervention cures chronic illness
options.D: Being relatively fast and cost-effective to carry out

explanation: Descriptive research is great for painting a picture or saving time and money, but proving a cure requires heavy-duty experimental trials! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h7)

question: How can a nurse manager use descriptive research on patient admission rates?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any further hospital documentation
options.B: To plan adequate staffing levels and shift rosters for busy periods
options.C: To test a new surgical procedure on incoming emergency patients
options.D: To prove that nurses cause patient illnesses during night shifts

explanation: Knowing peak admission times helps nurse managers schedule enough hands on deck so the ward runs smoothly and patients get great care. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h8)

question: A community health nurse conducts a survey to find out why mothers in a village do not bring children for immunization. What is the practical value of this study?

options.A: It guides the creation of a targeted local health education program
options.B: It forces every parent to pay a fine for missed immunizations
options.C: It proves that vaccines cure all known infectious diseases instantly
options.D: It replaces the need to administer vaccines in the clinic

explanation: By finding out the exact reasons for vaccine hesitancy, the nurse can design a friendly, localized outreach program that really helps the community. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h8)
